name: Jeroham
overview: Jeroham is a male Levite identified in Nehemiah 11:12 as the son of Pelaliah. His mention is brief, focusing primarily on his lineage within the tribe of Levi, which is significant for its priestly and temple service roles. No additional notes expand on his personal story or deeds.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroham means 'he will be compassionate.' This proper name, while not indicated as given directly by God, reflects a meaningful Hebrew attribute that may characterize his identity or the hopes of his family.
familyAndRelationships: Jeroham is explicitly identified as the son of Pelaliah. Additionally, it is inferred that Adaiah is his father, establishing a familial line within the Levite tribe. Scripture does not record further family details beyond these relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroham's significance lies in his inclusion among the Levites during the post-exilic period, highlighting the restoration of temple service and worship in Jerusalem. His lineage as the son of Pelaliah situates him within the priestly community essential for maintaining Israel's covenantal worship. Though details are sparse, his mention preserves the continuity of God's faithful servants in the rebuilding of the nation.
